definition: CellCognition is a free open-source computational framework for quantitative analysis of high-throughput fluorescence microscopy (time-lapse) images in the field of bioimage informatics and systems microscopy.
details: The CellCognition framework uses image processing, computer vision and machine learning techniques for single-cell tracking and classification of cell morphologies. This enables measurements of temporal progression of cell phases, modeling of cellular dynamics and generation of phenotype map.

explainer.lead: CellCognition is a free, open-source framework that turns high-throughput time-lapse fluorescence microscopy images into quantitative descriptions of individual cells. By following cells and classifying their changing shapes, it helps researchers study cell phases, cellular dynamics and patterns of phenotypes.

tiers.eli5: Imagine watching a crowd in a series of photos and trying to follow each person while noting what they are doing. CellCognition does something similar for cells: it follows each one through microscope images and records how its appearance changes. This helps scientists see how cells move through different phases and how groups of cells behave.
tiers.practitioner: CellCognition is applied to high-throughput, time-lapse fluorescence microscopy data, combining image processing and computer vision with machine learning. A typical workflow tracks individual cells, classifies their morphologies and derives phase progression, cellular dynamics or phenotype maps. Its outputs depend on the quality of tracking and morphology classification, so these stages should be checked before drawing quantitative conclusions.
tiers.paperLevel: CellCognition is a computational framework for quantitative bioimage analysis: given high-throughput fluorescence time-lapse images, it applies image processing, computer vision and machine learning to produce single-cell trajectories and morphology classifications. These representations support measurements of temporal cell-phase progression, models of cellular dynamics and phenotype maps. It is an analysis framework rather than a single tracking or classification algorithm.

explainer.example: A laboratory records fluorescence images of the same cell population at successive time points. CellCognition follows each cell through the image sequence and labels its morphology, allowing the researchers to measure how cells progress through phases and to summarise differences between cell behaviours in a phenotype map.

explainer.intuition: A time-lapse microscopy experiment contains more than a collection of cell pictures: it records how each cell changes over time. CellCognition makes that information measurable by linking observations into single-cell tracks and assigning morphology classes along those tracks.
howItWorks: Take high-throughput fluorescence microscopy images captured over time.
Use image processing and computer vision to analyse the cells in the images.
Track individual cells across frames and classify their morphologies using machine learning techniques.
Combine the tracks and classifications to measure cell-phase progression, model cellular dynamics and generate phenotype maps.
explainer.whyItMatters: It converts large time-lapse image collections into cell-level quantitative measurements that would be difficult to assemble by visual inspection alone. Those measurements connect changes in cell appearance with temporal behaviour and population-level phenotype patterns.
misconceptions: It is not just an image viewer: its purpose is quantitative analysis of microscopy image sequences.
It is not a single machine-learning model, but a framework combining image processing, computer vision and machine learning.
A morphology classification is not, by itself, a complete model of cellular dynamics; tracks and classifications are combined for that analysis.
